title: MasterGraph
description: Cross-book synthesis graph — the Syntopical layer of Adler's four levels. Composed from one or more BookGraph documents (schema/book-graph.schema.json) plus purpose-built syntopical nodes/edges that do not belong to any single book. This is the paid/differentiated layer: 'many books, one understanding'.

sourceBooks.description: book.id values (from BookGraph documents) included in this master graph.

questions.description: Step 1 of syntopical reading: frame your own question. Each question is a lens the user (or curator) poses, answered by pulling relevant nodes from multiple books.

prompt.description: e.g. 'What creates a sense of meaning?'

answeringNodeIds.description: Node ids (namespaced book:type:slug) across one or more BookGraphs that bear on this question.

vocabularyClusters.description: Step 3 of syntopical reading: build a shared vocabulary. Groups vocabulary-type nodes from different books that name the same or overlapping concept, even under different terms.

canonicalTerm.description: The unifying term the product surfaces, e.g. 'meaning-making'.

termsByBook.description: How each source book names/frames this concept in its own vocabulary.

conflictClusters.description: Step 4 of syntopical reading: find the point of conflict. Explicit modeling of where books disagree or emphasize differently on the same question — the highest-value, hardest-to-automate content in the whole product.

questionId.description: Optional link to a questions[] entry this conflict is about.

stance.description: One-line summary of this book's position, e.g. 'Suffering is meaningless unless transformed by choice.'

crossEdges.description: Direct node-to-node edges spanning different books, using the answers_question / shares_vocabulary_with / conflicts_with / supports relations from book-graph.schema.json's edge.relation enum.
